svg.text: Newton's isothermal vs Laplace adiabatic correction
Newton: B_T = P → v = √(P/ρ) ≈ 280 m/s (air, STP) – too low
Assumed T constant, heat flows during compression – wrong, process is rapid, adiabatic
Laplace: B_S = γ P → v = √(γP/ρ) = √(γRT/M) ≈ 331 m/s at 0°C, 343 m/s at 20°C
γ = Cp/Cv = 1.40 for diatomic gas. Adiabatic, no heat exchange during acoustic cycle
v ∝ √T, independent of P at fixed T
Humid air lighter M_eff ↓ → v ↑ (~0.3% rise)
Valid: ideal gas, f ≪ collision freq (~GHz), small amplitude
